chnischel.name: Karl Marx Monument (Nischel)
chnischel.slogan: A 40-tonne bronze head that locals simply call the Nischel.
chnischel.by: Karl Marx and Friedrich Engels, The Communist Manifesto, 1848 (carved behind the monument)

chgoeltzschtal.name: Göltzsch Viaduct
chgoeltzschtal.slogan: Twenty-six million bricks, stacked into a valley-wide stairway.
chgoeltzschtal.line: Built between 1846 and 1851, it is 78 metres high and counted the largest brick-built bridge in the world.

chaugustusburg.name: Augustusburg Castle
chaugustusburg.slogan: A Renaissance hunting lodge crowning the Schellenberg hilltop.
chaugustusburg.line: Elector Augustus built it from 1568 to 1572 on a hill 516 metres high, and it now also houses a motorcycle museum.

chfreibergdom.name: Freiberg Cathedral
chfreibergdom.slogan: Silver-town splendour, from Golden Gate to Silbermann organ.
chfreibergdom.line: Despite the name it was never a bishop's seat, yet nine Saxon rulers were buried in its choir after 1541.

chgunzenhauser.name: Museum Gunzenhauser
chgunzenhauser.slogan: Otto Dix's sharp eye in a former bank of New Objectivity.
chgunzenhauser.line: Opened in 2007 in a 1928-30 Sparkasse building, it holds 290 works by Otto Dix.
